sources.title: Dockery Armory, PTRD-41 (Degtyaryov 14.5x114mm anti-tank rifle), technical data sheet, ref. CODE 03-125-941

twists.locator: Data sheet field 'RIFLING (TYPE & TWIST)': '8-Grooves, Right hand twist, 1 turn in 45.5 cm (17.91 in)'. 45.5 cm = 455 mm, and 17.91 in x 25.4 = 454.9 mm. PROVENANCE: a published collector/reference data sheet for the PTRD-41, not a state document. The same pitch is stated for the cartridge in the English Wikipedia infobox (lead only). The 8-groove, right-hand direction is corroborated by the Russian KPVT technical description ('Внутри ствол имеет канал с восемью нарезами, вьющимися слева вверх направо' - the bore has eight grooves curving from left up to the right, no pitch given) and by Tank Encyclopedia ('The barrel had eight riflings'). No national standard, proof-house sheet or military manual giving the pitch was found.
twists.note: 8-Grooves, Right hand twist, 1 turn in 45.5 cm (17.91 in)

twists.locator: Wikipedia infobox: 'rifling = 1:8.66 in (220 mm)'. 8.66 in x 25.4 = 220.0 mm.
twists.grade_note: Tier 5 compilation. No national standard, proof-house sheet or military manual giving the pitch was found. Sanity check: an intermediate 7 mm service round of the late 1940s in a 1:8.66 twist band is physically ordinary, so the figure is accepted at grade claimed and never displaces a stronger source.
twists.blocker: No cartridge record exists for this round, so the twist cannot attach to one. It never entered service, so neither the CIP nor the SAAMI register holds it. A record needs citable case dimensions; none was found at tier 1-4, so the row waits rather than inventing them.

leads.reason: Wikipedia infobox: 'rifling = 455 mm (1 in 17.91 in)', with 8 grooves. A wiki is a lead only. It agrees with the tier 3 Dockery data sheet carried on the twist row above, so the row is graded by the Dockery source, and the wiki is recorded here as the independent corroboration.

Wikipedia infobox: 'rifling = 1:8.66 in (220 mm)'. This is the only source found that gives a pitch, and a wiki-only figure is a lead, so no twist row is written. No national standard, military manual, proof-house sheet, Cartridges of the World entry, Jane's entry or DTIC report stating the .280 British twist was found. Searched and found no pitch: DTIC report (Development and Proof Services, Aberdeen Proving Grounds, 5 June 1950, Ninth Report of Project TS2-2015, Vol. I, 239 pp.), the Rifle No.9 Mk.1 (EM-2) user handbook (OCR, no rifling data), rifleman.org.uk EM-2 page, municion.org 7x43 catalogue pages, and Koll/russianammo.org.
